findings.title: No privacy notice or recorded legal basis at the GitHub OAuth consent surface
findings.description: The /auth/github/login endpoint redirects users to GitHub without any privacy notice, data-collection disclosure, or documented legal basis. Repo-wide grep for privacy|LGPD|GDPR|consent across .rs/.md/.html/.js returns zero hits in registry code or docs. The registry processes personal data (GitHub login + numeric id, oauth.rs:70-74) upon login and persists it durably (storage_sqlite.rs:100-105 users table).
findings.root_cause: OAuth flow implemented as pure engineering surface (T57 Track F) with no privacy-UX or legal-basis step; MVP scope never included notice/consent artifacts.
findings.impact: Once deployed, LGPD Art. 9 (transparency) and GDPR Arts. 12-14 require a notice at or before collection; absence would be a compliance defect at launch. Today severity is LOW: undeployed (default bind 127.0.0.1:7878, lib.rs:127; invite-only allowlist default-on, lib.rs:120,243-248), so no production processing of Brazil/EU data subjects occurs.
findings.recommendation: Before public deployment: (1) serve a privacy notice (identity data collected: GitHub login+id; purpose: publish auth + author attribution; retention; controller contact; rights channel) linked from the login endpoint and README; (2) document the legal basis (likely contract execution LGPD Art. 7 V / GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)) in a PRIVACY.md; (3) record basis per processing purpose.

fix_examples.after: Ok((axum::http::StatusCode::FOUND, [(LOCATION, url.as_str()), (SET_COOKIE, cookie), (LINK, "</privacy>; rel=\"privacy-policy\"")]).into_response()) // plus GET /privacy route serving PRIVACY.md

findings.fix_guide: 1) Add PRIVACY.md at repo root (data collected, purposes, retention, controller email). 2) In oauth.rs login(), append a LINK header pointing at /privacy. 3) Add GET /privacy route in lib.rs::app(). 4) Add launch-checklist item gating public deployment on notice + basis review.

effort_estimate.breakdown: notice authoring 90m; /privacy route + LINK header 30m; legal-basis doc 30m; tests + review 30m

detection_method.query: Select-String across repo for privacy|LGPD|GDPR|consent returned 0 matches in buff-registry

confidence.rationale: Zero-match grep over full repo plus full read of the login handler; absence is directly observable.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: MVP/undeployed status explicitly documented (root AGENTS.md v1.28 registry MVP, loopback bind, allowlist default), so severity capped at low; the gap itself (no notice text exists anywhere) is factual.

findings.title: No data subject rights endpoints (access/export/rectification/erasure) for persisted GitHub identity
findings.description: The complete route table (lib.rs:279-302) contains only publish, package, download, resolve, badges, stats, search, multipart publish/download, health, ready, and four auth routes (login/callback/logout/whoami). No endpoint lets a user access, export, correct, or delete their stored personal data. OAuth logout deletes only the session row; users table rows (storage_sqlite.rs:100-105) persist in durable WAL SQLite with no deletion code path anywhere in the crate.
findings.root_cause: Registry MVP (T126) and T57 auth hardening scoped storage + OAuth only; DSAR tooling was never a task.
findings.impact: If deployed, data subjects could not exercise LGPD Art. 18 (access, correction, portability, deletion) or GDPR Arts. 15-20 self-service; the operator would need manual SQL, and erasure of github_login referenced by versions.author/org_members FKs would be error-prone. LOW today: undeployed, defaults to ephemeral in-memory storage.
findings.recommendation: Pre-launch: implement GET /api/v1/account/export and DELETE /api/v1/account (erases/anonymizes users row, sessions, allowlist entry, NULLs versions.author), or at minimum document a manual DSAR runbook in PRIVACY.md.
findings.fix_guide: 1) Add Storage::delete_user(github_id) to the trait, both backends (DELETE sessions by user_id; DELETE allowlist; UPDATE versions SET author=NULL WHERE author=login; DELETE org_members; DELETE users). 2) Add handlers behind session auth. 3) Integration tests. Alternatively ship the manual runbook as interim control.

effort_estimate.breakdown: trait method + 2 impls 150m; handlers + routes 90m; FK/anonymization edge cases 120m; tests 90m; docs 30m

detection_method.query: Select-String '.route(' on lib.rs enumerated all 15 routes; none implement access/export/delete of user data

confidence.rationale: Route table exhaustive and small; absence verified by full enumeration plus grep for delete/export primitives in both storage backends.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: AGENTS.md MVP conventions: in-memory default backend and undeployed status cap severity at low; finding states factual absence without overstating current exposure.

findings.title: GitHub OAuth architecture transfers personal data to GitHub Inc. (US) with no documented transfer basis
findings.description: OAuth constants hardwire GitHub endpoints (github.com/login/oauth/authorize, api.github.com/user). Login involves a third-country (US) processor: the user's GitHub identity (login + numeric id) is fetched from GitHub Inc. infrastructure and persisted locally. Data minimization is good - scope read:user only, no email/profile scopes, only two fields deserialized.
findings.root_cause: GitHub OAuth is the chosen identity provider (T57 Track F); international flow is inherent to the architecture, but no transfer documentation accompanies it.
findings.impact: Posture fact, LOW for the undeployed tool: once operated (from Brazil or EU), the transfer must be covered by the privacy notice and a transfer mechanism (LGPD Arts. 33-36, e.g. ANPD SCCs; GDPR Ch. V - EU-US DPF may cover GitHub as certified entity).
findings.recommendation: In the pre-launch PRIVACY.md (AUD-RGD-001), document: recipient (GitHub Inc., US), data transferred (login + id), and the transfer basis; verify GitHub DPF status or execute ANPD SCCs. No code change strictly required (OAuthConfig already parameterizes endpoints).

fix_examples.after: pub const DEFAULT_USER_URL: &str = "https://api.github.com/user"; // PRIVACY.md: identity (login,id) transferred to GitHub Inc. (US) under SCC/DPF

findings.fix_guide: 1) PRIVACY.md international-transfer section naming GitHub Inc., the two fields, and the legal mechanism. 2) Pre-launch checklist line verifying GitHub DPF certification status. 3) No runtime change needed.

effort_estimate.breakdown: transfer section drafting 40m; DPF status verification 20m

detection_method.query: Select-String 'github.com|api.github.com' in oauth.rs located hardcoded cross-border endpoints

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path "crates\buff-registry\src\oauth.rs" -Pattern "github\.com|api\.github\.com|read:user"; Select-String -Path "crates\buff-registry\src\storage_sqlite.rs" -Pattern "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO users" -Context 0,2

confidence.rationale: Endpoints and transferred fields directly verified in code; the legal-mechanism judgment is documented as a posture note, not a code defect.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Framed as a documented posture fact per audit instructions; data minimization verified; MVP/undeployed status per AGENTS.md caps severity at low.
